title: MirrorGeneralizedSmooth.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable convex minimization on E, with an attained minimum; no strong convexity of f is assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Queries return the exact derivative in the dual space, for every history and seed.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Exact minimizer of v(u)+Bψ(u,z) over E. Gradient and prox queries share the single counted oracle budget; function values are unavailable.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Continuous derivative g satisfies ‖g(x)−g(y)‖≤(L0+L1 M)‖x−y‖ whenever its norm is bounded by M throughout the segment. Public parameters satisfy L0>0 and L1≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: Arbitrary norm and differentiable mirror function with Bψ(y,x)≥‖y−x‖²/2. A minimizer satisfies Bψ(x*,x0)≤D and f(x0)−f(x*)≤Δ, with public D,Δ>0; the mirror function is hidden behind the prox oracle.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real normed vector space.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point in E satisfying f(output)−f(x*)≤ε for a minimizer x*, with ε>0. ε is excluded from publicInput, so the algorithm is independent of the requested tolerance.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap bound holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Gradient-dependent segment smoothness combined with general Bregman geometry and a joint exact gradient/prox budget is a meaningful variant of standard smooth convex optimization.

descriptionHtml:
Generalized Smooth Convex Mirror Geometry

We minimize a differentiable convex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real normed space E. The function f is (L0,L1)-smooth, with L0>0 and L1≥0. A differentiable mirror function ψ:E→R induces a Bregman divergence Bψ dominating half the squared norm. A given point x0∈E satisfies Bψ(x⋆,x0)≤D and f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ for a minimizer x⋆, where D,Δ>0. The oracle returns exact derivatives and Bregman proximal minimizers. For ε>0, the goal is f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). Write E∗ for the continuous dual of E. Derivatives ∇f(x) and ∇ψ(x) belong to E∗, and their norms are the induced operator norms ∥⋅∥op. Define Bψ(u,z)=ψ(u)−ψ(z)−∇ψ(z)[u−z]. The algorithm receives E, L0, L1, D, Δ, and x0; the tolerance ε may enter only the oracle-call budget.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and generalized smoothness). The function f is everywhere Fréchet differentiable, its derivative is continuous, and f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y),x,y∈E,t∈[0,1]. Its (L0,L1)-smoothness means that, for every x,y∈E and M∈R, ∥∇f(x+θ(y−x))∥op≤Mfor all θ∈[0,1]⟹∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥op≤(L0+L1M)∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Mirror geometry and proximal access). The function ψ is everywhere Fréchet differentiable and satisfies Bψ(y,x)≥12∥y−x∥2,x,y∈E. For every z∈E and v∈E∗, a selected proximal minimizer exists: proxψ(z,v)∈argminu∈E⁡{v[u]+Bψ(u,z)}.

Assumption 3 (Initial bounds). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,Bψ(x⋆,x0)≤D,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. It also returns proxψ(z,v) on a query (z,v)∈E×E∗. Both types of queries are exact, may be made anywhere in their stated domains, and count toward a single total oracle-call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯∈E must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s., where the global minimizer x⋆ is fixed independently of the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Convex differentiable f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real normed space, with continuous gradient satisfying ∥g(x)−g(y)∥∗≤(L0+L1M)∥x−y∥ whenever ∥g∥∗≤M on [x,y]. A differentiable mirror satisfies Bψ(u,z)≥∥u−z∥2/2; exact gradient and Bregman-prox oracles are supplied. A minimizer x∗ satisfies Bψ(x∗,x0)≤D and f(x0)−f(x∗)≤Δ, with L0,D,Δ,ε>0, L1≥0. Target: f(xK)−f(x∗)≤ε almost surely.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

open Set

namespace LongTails.Setups.MirrorGeneralizedSmooth

open OracleTemplate

def SegmentSmooth {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] (g : E → F) (L0 L1 : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y M, (∀ θ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖g (x + θ • (y - x))‖ ≤ M) →
    ‖g x - g y‖ ≤ (L0 + L1 * M) * ‖x - y‖

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  D : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.finiteE

structure Params extends Public where
  ε : ℝ

inductive Query (p : Public) where
  | gradient (x : p.E)
  | prox (z : p.E) (v : p.E →L[ℝ] ℝ)

inductive Reply (p : Public) where
  | gradient (v : p.E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
  | prox (x : p.E)

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  grad : p.E → p.E →L[ℝ] ℝ
  ψ : p.E → ℝ
  mirrorGrad : p.E → p.E →L[ℝ] ℝ
  prox : p.E → (p.E →L[ℝ] ℝ) → p.E

def bregman {p : Public} (I : Instance p) (u z : p.E) : ℝ :=
  I.ψ u - I.ψ z - I.mirrorGrad z (u - z)

def proxObjective {p : Public} (I : Instance p) (z : p.E) (v : p.E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (u : p.E) : ℝ := v u + bregman I u z

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query := Query
  Reply := Reply
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ p.L1 ∧ 0 < p.D ∧ 0 < p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I oracle :=
    (∀ history seed x, oracle.answer history (0, .gradient x) seed = .gradient (I.grad x)) ∧
    (∀ history seed z v, oracle.answer history (0, .prox z v) seed = .prox (I.prox z v)) ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ univ I.f ∧
    (∀ x, HasFDerivAt I.f (I.grad x) x) ∧
    Continuous I.grad ∧
    SegmentSmooth I.grad p.L0 p.L1 ∧
    (∀ x, HasFDerivAt I.ψ (I.mirrorGrad x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖y - x‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ bregman I y x) ∧
    (∀ z v, IsMinOn (proxObjective I z v) univ (I.prox z v)) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn I.f univ xstar ∧ bregman I xstar p.x0 ≤ p.D ∧
      I.f p.x0 - I.f xstar ≤ p.Δ)
  successful p I output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn I.f univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), I.f (output ω) - I.f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.MirrorGeneralizedSmooth
